Mr. MA Quiyum, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Appellants. (In all the appeals). 
Mr. Zulfiqur Bulbul Chowdhury, Advocate instructed by Mr N I Bhuiyan, Advocate-On-Record --------- For the Respondents. (In all the appeals)

Mohammad Selim and others ------- Appellant. (In all the appeals).
Vs.
Mohammad Ismail Sowdagar and other -------- Respondents. (In all the appeals).
case_source: (From the judgment and decree dated 12.06.2008, passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision Nos. 2408 of 2003, 2418 of 2003, 2416 of 2003 and 5134 of 2003).
full_judgment:
MIRZA HUSSAIN HAIDER, J.: These 4(four) civil appeals, by leave, are directed against the judgment and order dated 12.06.2008 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision Nos. 2408 of 2003, 2418 of 2003, 2416 of 2003 and 5134 of 2003 making all the four Rules absolute and thereby setting aside the judgment and decree dated 22.01.2003 passed by the learned Additional District Judge (in charge), 5th Court, Chittagong in Other Class Appeal No. 53 of 1990 heard along with Other Class Appeal No. 47 of 1990 dismissing the said two appeals and affirming the judgment and decree dated 07.01.1990 passed in Other Class Suit No. 318 of 1984 heard along with Other Class Suit No. 54 of 1984.

2. In all the 4(four) appeals fact being similar and the question of law involved being the same all were heard together and disposed of by this common judgment.

3. Short facts, necessary for disposal of the aforesaid appeals are:

4. The respondent No. 1 herein (Md. Ismail Sowdagar) on 09.06.1983 instituted Other Class Suit No. 181 of 1983 (subsequently re-numbered as Other Class Suit No. 318 of 1984) in the 2nd Court of Munsif (Now Assistant Judge) Satkania, Chittagong for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and partition of his share in respect of 2 konto 9 teel of land out of 1.80 acre along with the shop room situated thereon in R.S. Khatian No. 439, R.S. Plot No.2353 of Mouza Adhunagar. He also prayed for declaration that all order or decree dated 30.4.1983 passed in Village Court Case No. 9 of 1983 filed by defendant No.1 (Md. Selim) along with the entire proceedings of the said case is illegal, without jurisdiction, void and as such the plaintiff is not bound by the same.

5. It is stated that the aforesaid 1.80 acre of land along with other lands originally belonged to Ali Hossain, who died leaving four sons, Abdur Rahman, Mokbul Ali, Abdur Rashid and Abdul Mojid and one daughter, Momjan Bibi who inherited the same. Momjan Bibi inherited the share measuring an area of 0.02 acre and Abdur Rahman and other three brothers got 0.04 acre of land each. Abdur Rahman died leaving behind two sons Mostafizur Rahman and Mujahar Miah to inherit his share. Mustafizur Rahman transferred 0.03 acre of land to Ashab Mia and Bodiul Alam by deed dated 21.07.1965. Ashab Mia thereafter constructed a temporary shop room with corrugated iron sheet (C.I. sheet) roofing. Subsequently he transferred the same to Ismail Sowdagar (present respondent No.1) by deed dated 17.02.1982. The heirs of Mustafizur Rahman (the present appellants) being inimical with him over the Union Parishad election obtained a collusive order in Village Court Case No.9 of 1983. Hence Ismail Sowdagar filed this suit.

6. The suit was contested by defendant No. 1 Md. Selim (appellant No. 1 of Civil Appeal No. 500 of 2009) by filing written statement in one set and defendant Nos. 4- 10 other heirs of Mustafizur Rahman (appellants Nos. 2-6 and respondent No. 2 respectively of Civil Appeal No. 500 of 2008) by filing another set of written statement. Both sets of defendants denied the material allegations made in the plaint stating inter-alia that they instituted Other Class Suit No. 54 of 1984 (originally Other Class Suit No. 264 of 1984) in the Court of Assistant Judge, Lohagara, against Ismail Sowdagor and others for declaration of their title in respect of the self same suit property and further declaration that by registered deed No. 826 dated 17.02.1982, allegedly executed by Ashab Mia, the defendant No. 1 (Md. Ismail Sowdagar) did not purchase the shop room and as such the said Ismail Sowdagar did not get the shop by purchase. Subsequently the plaintiff amended some of the paragraphs of the plaint along with the prayer and added the prayer for eviction of the defendant No. 1, Md. Ismail Sowdagar from the suit land. So the suit was a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession upon eviction of defendant No. 1.

7. In their written statement, filed in Other Suit No. 318 of 1984, the aforesaid defendants re-irritated their case as stated in the plaint of Other Suit No. 54 of 1984. Their case in short is that the aforesaid 1.80 acre of land of RS Khatian No. 439 of Mouza Abunagar under Lohagora Police Station belonged to Abdur Rahman, Mokbul Ali, Abdur Rashid and Abdul Mojid all sons of Ali Hossain in equal 4(four) annas share each. Abdur Rahman died leaving behind two sons, namely, Mostafizur Rahman and Mozaher Mia. By deed dated 08.12.1952 Mokbul Ali (brother of Abdur Rahman) transferred his share of .45 acres to Mustafizur Rahman and by another deed dated 19.02.1952 one Abdul Bari Master also transferred .11 acre of land to Mustafizur Rahman. Thus Mustafizur Rahman, became the owner of 0.22 +0.45 +0.11 =0.79 acres of land by way of inheritance and purchase. Thereafter Mostafizur Rahman transferred 0.3 acre of land, recorded as Nal Land, to Ashab Mia and Bodiul Alam. Out of the suit lands some were acquired by the Government for Roads and Highways and the remaining lands have been correctly recorded in B.S. Khatian. Mustafizur Rahman constructed one corrugated iron roofing temporary shop room, measuring 16/12 cubits, on the north-western corner of R.S. Plot No. 2353 and possessed the same for some time and thereafter he let that out the same to different persons and lastly to the Ismail Sowdagar (respondent no.1) in 1974 which was recorded as plot No.6302 of B.S. Khatian No. 2271. Mostafizur Rahman died leaving behind wife Moslema Khatun, 3(three) sons Md. Selim, Solaiman, Nur Mohammad, and 4 daughters Monowara Begum, Jamuna Khatun, Halima Khatun and Janu Bibi(defendants No. 1 to 8 of Suit No. 318 of 1984). The respondent No. 1, Ismail Sowdagar, had been paying rents to Md. Selim and others but subsequently with a malafide motive created a forged deed allegedly to have been executed by Ashab Miah and stopped payment rents. Consequently Md. Selim (the appellant No. 1) lodged a complaint before the Village Court in Village Court Case No.9 of 1983 wherein Ismail Sowdagar has been found to be the tenant of Md. Selim and others and as such liable to pay arrear rent of Tk. 998.50 to be landlords. It is further stated that the deed, allegedly executed by Ashab Mia in respect of the said shop room by which Ismail Sowdagor claims title, is fraudulent and he has not acquired any title on the basis of the said deed nor the land transferred by Ashab Miah to Ismail Sowdagar attracts the suit shop which was recorded in plot Nos. 6293 and 6395 of B.S. Khatian Nos. 551 and 82. Hence they prayed that Other Class Suit No. 318 of 1984 filed by Ismail Sowdagar should be dismissed and Other Class Suit No. 54 of 1984 filed by them should be decreed.

8. Defendants No. 11 and 12 and defendant No. 25 of Other Class Suit No. 318 of 1984, who are also defendants in Other Class Suit No. 54 of 1984 also filed their written statements. Defendants No. 11 and 12 admitted that Ismail Sowdagar is a tenant under Md. Selim and others. They claimed Ali Hossain, the predecessor of Mostafizur Rahman and Md. Selim and others had no daughter named Momjan Bibi and the respondent No. 1 (Ismail Sowdagar) is not entitled to get any relief in his suit who was inducted as a tenant in the suit shop premises and subsequently upon collusively creating a deed claimed that he purchased the shop from Ashab Miah. Hence Suit No. 318 of 1984 should be dismissed. On the other hand defendant No. 25 contended that Ali Hossain had one daughter named Manjan Bibi along with his aforesaid four sons, (Abdur Rahman and others) but wrongly her name has not been recorded in RS Khatian. Defendant No. 25 inherited and purchased 61/2(six and half) gondas of land and constructed a shop room which she posses by letting out. Other defendants who contested the suit made their claims and counter claims in respect of the suit property along with other properties and also claimed their sahams.

9. The trial Court upon hearing both the suits analogously dismissed Other Class Suit No. 318 of 1984 and decreed Other Class Suit No. 54 of 1984 by judgment and decree dated 07.01.1990.

10. Ismail Sowdagor (present respondent No. 1) being aggrieved by the said judgment and decrees preferred Other Class Appeal No. 53 of 1990 against the judgment and decree passed in his Other Class Suit No. 318 of 1984 and also preferred Other Class Appeal No. 47 of 1990 against the judgment and decree passed in Other Class Suit No. 54 of 1984. Defendant No. 25 of Other Class Suit No. 318 of 1984 preferred cross objection in Other Class Appeal No. 53 of 1990. All the aforesaid appeals and the cross objection were heard analogously and the learned Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Chittagong by his judgment and decree dated 21.01.2003 dismissed both the appeals as well as the cross objection affirming the judgment and decrees of the trial Court.

11. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree of the Court of appeal below the present respondent No. 1 (Ismail Sowdagor) filed two civil revisions before the High Court Division, being Civil Revision No. 2416 of 2003 (challenging the judgment of Other Class Appeal No. 47 of 1990 arising out of Other Class Suit No. 54 of 1984) and Civil Revision No. 2418 of 2003 (challenging the judgment of Other Class Appeal No. 53 of 1990 arising out of Other Class Suit No. 318 of 1984). On the other hand defendant No. 25 of Other Class Suit No. 318 of 1984 filed Civil Revision No. 2408 of 2003 against the judgment and order passed in his cross objection and the heirs of Ashab Miah, filed Civil Revision No. 5134 of 2003 against the judgment and decree passed in Other Class Appeal No. 47 of 1990 and obtained four Rules.

12. All the 4(four) Rules were heard analogously and a Single Bench of the High Court Division by its judgment and order dated 12.6.2008 made all the 4(four) Rules absolute and set aside the judgment and decree of the courts below and also remanded the suits to the trial Court for holding fresh trial.

13. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order of the High Court Division in the aforesaid 4(four) Rules, Md. Selim and others (plaintiffs of Other Class Suit No. 54 of 1984 and defendants of Other Class Suit No. 318 of 1984) filed four Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal being Civil Petition No. 2186, 2187, 2200 and 2201 all of 2008 and obtained leave giving rise to these 4(four) civil appeals.

14. Mr. M.A. Quiyum, senior counsel, appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that Ismail Sawdagar having appeared before the Village Court and having paid up the arrear rent of Tk.998.50 to Md. Selim, in compliance of order passed therein without challenging the authority of the said court, and both the Courts below concurrently found that to be admission of tenancy the finding of the High Court Division that the said Court had no authority to deal with the case is a wrong finding and thereby erroneously made the Rules absolute.

15. He next submits that the finding of the High Court Division that the share of the parties in the suit land is admitted is contrary to the concurrent finding of both the courts below. The said Courts specifically held that 'upon collusively and fraudulently inserting different B.S. Khatian number and Plot numbers in the said three kabalas, Ismail Sowdagor claimed to have purchased the suit land, as evident from the evidence of PWs. 1-3 and exhibit H-H2 which clearly proved that the schedule of the said illegal kabalas, executed by Ashab Miah, and the Suit shop are completely different.

16. He next submits that the High Court Division erred in law in not considering the concurrent findings of the courts below that 'Ismail Sawdagor failed to prove his induction as a tenant in the suit land in 1967 by Ashab Miah through Exhibit-4, which is false, fabricated and a created afterthought document'. He further submits that both the courts below concurrently found that 'Exhibit 2, 2(ka) and 2(kha) are collusive and fraudulent documents and no consideration having been passed the same cannot be the basis of any title and that there was no existence of Manjan Bibi'. But the High Court Division without reversing the said findings made the Rule absolute which is erroneous and as such liable to be set aside.

17. Lastly, he submits, that on the face of Section 116 of the Evidence Act a tenant is not entitled to claim title without surrendering possession to the land lord as such the findings of the High Court Division that 'Ismail Sawdagor purchased the suit shop which was in his possession is erroneous and not sustainable in law. Apart from the above submissions, according to Mr. Quiyum when all the issues were decided by both the courts below upon proper appreciation of evidence on record remanding both the suits back to the trial court, without reversing all the findings of the courts below, the High Court Division committed error of law and as such the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside.

18. On the other hand, Mr. Zulfiquar Bulbul Chowdhury, learned advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents in all the appeals submits that PWs 1 to 3 in their deposition admitted the respondent No.1, Ismail Sowdagar, as a co-sharer in the suit land which is also proved by Exhibits H to H-2 and Exhibit-2. Moreover tenancy being determined by notice dated 04.12.1985 under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, the claim of Mohammad Selim in Other Class Suit No. 54 of 1984 for eviction is liable to be dismissed for want of proper and lawful notice. Again after acquisition of part of the land and transfer by the predecessor of the plaintiff-appellants no property is left with them. On the other hand the judgment and order of the Village Court dated 13.4.1983 passed under sections 427/340/349 of the Penal Code is without jurisdiction and as such the same cannot be the basis for decreeing Other Suit No. 54 of 1984 and dismissing Other Suit No. 318 of 1984. These vital aspects of fact and law were not considered by the Courts below which the High Court Division rightly pointed out and accordingly made the Rules absolute. Thus the impugned judgment does not call for any interference by this Court.

19. According to Mr. Chowdhury, Exhibit XII, the death certificate of Manjan Bibi, clearly shows that she was the daughter of Ali Hossain, and as such she inherited 0.20 acre of land in the suit plot from her father Ali Hossain. But both the Courts below misconstrued Exhibit-XII and came to a wrong decision that she is not the heir/daughter of Ali Hossain and thereby rejected the prayer for saham by defendant No.25 though her name was recorded in BS Khatian No. 1546 in respect of her share in the suit land. Considering the genealogy and materials on record the High Court Division rightly found that defendant No. 25, being heir of Ali Hossain, through Monzan Bibi, inherited .07 acres of land and as such she is entitled to get the same as her saham in the suit land. All these aspects and documents (Exts. Ito XII) categorically prove the right, title and possession of the respondent No.1(Ismail Sawdagar) and defendant No. 25 (Hafeza Khatun) in RS Khatian No. 2353. The courts below having failed to consider these aspects in its true perspective and the High Court Division having correctly assessed the materials on record rightly made all the Rules absolute and thereby sending the suits back to the trial Court, on remand, for fresh trial does not call for any interference.

20. On these backdrops we perused the materials on record including the judgment and order of the High Court Division as well as the judgment passed by the two courts below. It appears that both the courts below concurrently found that the present appellants successfully proved their title over the suit land and that the present respondent No. 1 was the tenant under them in respect of the suit shop wherein the present respondent No. 1 has no right, title and interest and he was a mere tenant under the present appellants and accordingly decreed the eviction suit being Other Class Suit No. 54 of 1984 filed by the present appellants and dismissed Other Class Suit No. 318 of 1984 for declaration of title and partition filed by the present respondent No. 1.

21. On consideration of all materials on record, as well as the evidence adduced by both the parties it appears that the two courts below found that the claim of Ismail Sowdagar (present respondent No. 1) is on the basis of Exhibit-1 and 2 the sale deeds of 1982 wherein the land described in the schedule do not tally with the land described in the schedule of the deed of purchase by Ashab Miah from Mostafizer Rahman in 1965. Again both the Courts below concurrently found that Exhibit 1 and 2 contains KBS Plot and Khatian number which appears to be in the name of the predecessor of the present appellant not in the name of Ashab Miah. The courts below further held that, all the witnesses admitted that Ismail Sowdagar was the tenant under Mustafizur Rahman whereas not a single witness, on behalf of the present respondents, admitted absolute possession of respondent No. 1 in the suit land. No document has been produced by the present respondents before the courts below to prove respondent No. 1’s possession or title in the suit/ shop. Thus the courts below came to a definite finding that Exhibit-1 and 2 by which the present respondent No. 1 claims title is vague and collusive and by virtue of the said documents the respondent No.1 did not acquire any right, title, interest and possession in the suit land and as such he cannot claim any saham in the suit land.

22. In respect of the claim of Hafeza Khatun, (defendant No. 25) the court of appeal below held that the name of Munzan Bibi, the alleged daughter of Ali Hossain, does not appear either in the R.S. or in the previous P.S. record nor the said defendant could prove her claim that Munjan Bibi was the daughter of Ali Hossain by any evidence, oral or documentary, to the satisfaction of the Court other than producing the death certificate and some other papers, which also have not been proved in accordance with law.

23. But the High Court Division, relying on the evidence of the husband of Hafeza Khatun (defendantno.25) came to a conclusion that since 'the learned Advocate for the plaintiff appellants did not give any suggestion to the husband of Hafeza Khatun as to the relationship between Hafeza Khatun and Md. Selim and other heirs and successors of late Ali Hossain, it has undoubtedly proved that Hafeza Khatun was one of the successors of Ali Hossain'. Basing on such finding as to the existence of such heir/successor it observed that 'the prevailing facts and circumstances of the instant case do not require any death or birth certificate'. Again in respect of eviction suit (Other Class Suit No. 54 of 1984) the High Court Division held that Md. Ismail Sowdagar, the defendant of this suit who is the plaintiff of partition suit (Other Suit No. 318 of 1984) claimed that the shop in which he has been running his business, belonged to him, as he purchased the same from Ashab Miah to whom the suit land was transferred by Mustafizur Rahman, the father of Md. Selim'. Thus the High Court Divsion found that "Md. Ismail Sowdagar has acquired right, title and possession in a part of the suit land wherein he has been running his business'.

24. In respect of the order of the Village Court the High Court Division observed that 'the Village Court has got no jurisdiction to try any criminal matter when the proceeding was initiated under sections 417/340/349 of the Penal Code and as such it committed illegality in converting the said case into a suit for eviction and thereby decided the same and passed a decree for realization of arrear rent. This is completely beyond the jurisdiction of the Village Court and the Courts below in decreeing the suit for eviction and dismissing the suit for partition, relying on the said order of the village court has committed gross illegality'.

25. In respect of title of Md. Selim and tenancy of Ismail Sowdagar under him, the High Court Division found the exhibited documents of Md. selim "not sufficient to establish such claim". It further observed 'after acquisition of part of the suit land by the Government, Md. Selim or his predecessor had no further share in the suit land. Since they sold rest of their land to others as claimed by Ismail Sowdagar'. These findings of the High Court are contrary to the concurrent findings of the courts below. Which as a revisional court cannot hold without observing that the courts below came to such finding without considering any document or upon misconstruing any evidence on record. The High Court Division rather failed to construe that Md. Selim become owner of 0.79 acre of land by inheritance and purchase out of which a portion of land was acquired by the government. Even after such acquisition in 1952 Md. Selim had some share in the suit land wherein the alleged shop which he rented out to Ismail Sowdagar is situated.

26. On the other hand in support of his claim, Ismail Sowdagar (the defendant) produced two information slips which have been marked as Exhibits-5 and 5A. The High Court Division observed that "the said two information slips were not considered by the Courts below. Had those been considered then claim and counter claim of the parties could easily be decided "because purchase of some land by Md. Ismail in the suit property cannot be denied". It is not understood as to how the High Court Division could come to such conclusion and relying on which evidence.

27. In respect of existence of Monjan Bibi claiming to be the daughter of late Ali Hossain, the High Court Division observed "as per my finding there is no scope to decide that Ali Hossain had no daughter named as Monjan Bibi and in presence of said daughter each heir of Ali Hossain will get .40 acre in their share because admittedly the quantum of the suit land is only 1.80 acre in the record". Accordingly the High Court Division found it just to send back the suit to the trial Court on remand to decide as per observation made in the judgment.

<u>28. On perusal of the materials on record including the judgments of the two Courts below it appears that both the Courts relying on both oral and documentary evidence came to a specific finding that Ismail Sowdagar failed to prove his title by way of purchase in 1982 from Ashab Miah, since the schedule of the deeds do not tally with the deed of purchase of Ashab Miah from Mustafiz. Both the Courts below also found that Md. Selim and others have been able to prove their title in the suit land and also succeeded in proving that Ismail Sowdagar was a tenant under them, who by means of a deed of 1982, procured from Ashab Miah, claimed title in the suit shop. This fact as it appears from the judgment of both the Courts below, is admitted by defendant No.25 Hajera Khatun. The High Court Division, on the face of such specific and concurrent finding erroneously came to the finding, without discussing any evidence and/or reversing such concurrent findings of the courts below rather relying on two information slips and on the disputed purchase deeds of Ismail Sowdagar came to a finding that he has title in the suit land. Such finding is not only error of law but also base on evidence because the revisional court reversed the concurrent finding of fact without pointing out as to what are the errors which led to occasioning failure of justice.</u>

29. One thing is to be kept in mind that two suits, one filed by Ismail Sowdagar for title and partition and the other, filed by Md. Selim and others initially for declaration and subsequently by amendment for declaration and eviction and recovery of khas possession. The subject matter of two suits are completely different. It is not denied by Ismail Sowdagar (the present respondent No. 1) that he entered into the suit shop as a tenant. The P.Ws. as well as the D.Ws. and defendant No. 25, Hafeza Khatun, all have admitted that Ismail Sowdagar is a tenant under Md. Selim and others. If the tenancy is proved the only question remains whether he is an ejectable tenant for non-payment of rent and/or when the tenant upon disowning the title of the landlord, claims himself to be the owner. Both the Courts below specifically disbelieved the sale deed executed by Ashab Miah to Ismail Showdagor as the plot number described in the schedule of the sale deed (Exhts 1 and 2 ) do not tally with Ashab Miah's deed of purchase from Mustafiz the predecessor of Md. Selim and others. The khatian numbers stated therein do not contain the name of Ashab Miah or that of Ismail Showdagor rather the same contains the name of Mustafiz, the predecessor of Md. Selim and others. Again the suit land sold to Ashab Miah by Mostafizur Rahman in 1965 appears to be completely a separate plot under B.S. Khatian Nos. 551 and 82, Plot Nos. 6293 and 6295 whereas the suit plot is Plot No. 2353. So there is no reason to hold that Ismail Sowdagar purchased the suit plot from Ashab Miah as Ashab did not purchase the same from Mostafiz. When the vendor does not have any title on a property and if the same is transferred to the vendee no title is transferred by such deed to the vendee. Thus Ismail Sowdagar did not get any title in the suit land. The courts below concurrently found the same. But the High Court Division without consideration this aspect passed the impugned judgment and order which is not in accordance with law.

30. In respect of jurisdiction of village court, upon which the courts below relied, it is to be noted that Ismail Showdagor without raising any objection submitted to the jurisdiction of the said court and in compliance of the order of the said court paid the arrear rents to the land lord Md. Selim without challenging the authority of the said court. When anyone submits to the jurisdiction of any court /authority and complies with the order of such court/ authority he is debarred from questioning the authority/ jurisdiction of the said court under the principle of acquiesce, waiver and estoppels. Thus the respondent No. 1 cannot claim that the village Court had no authority/jurisdiction to pass such order.

31. So far all the above discussions are concerned those relates to the eviction suit. Now question remains what could be the fate of the partition suit filed by respondent No. 1. In a suit for partition, the Court has to determine the title of a claimant. Unless a person has title on the suit land he cannot claim any sahams. But in the cases in hand the Courts below on proper assessment of the evidence on record came to a definite finding that Ismail Showdagor was a tenant under Md. Selim and others, which has also been admitted by Ismail Showdagor by paying rent pursuant to the decision of the village Court. Be that as it may since there are other parties who also prayed for their respective sahams and since the Court has ample power to look into the title of any claimant in a partition suit, the said suit may continue in accordance with law wherein the concerned Court will deter-mine the title of all the parties praying for their respective shams and decide the case in accordance with law.

32. Accordingly, we find merit in the submissions made by the learned Counsel for the appellants. Hence, all the four civil appeals are allowed. The Other Class Suit No. 54 of 1984 for eviction of Md. Ismail Sowdagar the tenant is decreed and the judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division in respect of this suit is hereby set aside upon restoring the judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge and affirmed by the learned Additional District judge, 5th court Chittagong. Other Suit No.318 of 1984, instituted by Ismail Showdagor for partition shall proceed in accordance with law by the trial Court as directed by the High Court Division.

33. However, there is no order as to costs.

End.
